notes.title: Monthly Development Update - July 2025
notes.notes:
This month has been all about momentum. Planets, missions, and the systems that tie it all together. Our third Planet (official name incoming) is well underway, with fresh terrain, environmental effects, and some seriously mind-bending rocks and trees. Facility design is expanding fast, and our mission system is starting to feel fully alive..



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/08654957339491d71802b7ee76f1a20396a5e5df.jpg"]

Players will notice smoother targeting, better feedback, new HUD elements, and dynamic music shifts that respond to gameplay. We’ve also implemented mission loading screens, real-time death drops, and refined how Facilities rotate on the Mission Map.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/61b1e0e0d5678bf2ee7f07811a029205e9d09ec5.jpg"]


Meanwhile, behind the scenes, we’ve been optimizing just about everything, from material meshes to how Facility maps stream in and out. Beamable now manages all mission and planet state data.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d8b71491f567b46a7ea049e2b020b5e1e2f27e18.jpg"]

And of course, with gamescom 2025 on the horizon, we’ve been laying the groundwork for a big showing, tightening our GTM plan, while we prepare for our closed Beta launch.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/7b36e33f805925b97ef06c687fb36cd0c93f96fd.jpg"]
Let’s get into it.

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - June 2025
notes.notes:
Another month in the bag here at Warped, and this month was heavily focused on gameplay and player experience. Gameplay, progression, maps, enemies, loadouts, and almost all other areas of where games become “fun” were leveled up this month. There was a point where everyone on the team started talking about how it suddenly was more fun and it felt rewarding to play. It wasn’t just testing, it was enjoyable.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/e7dda7104383594125b1822c7df4a4fdcd033e06.jpg"]

We’ve been aiming to reach this point in internal testing and development before moving on to our next phase, which involves bringing in outside testers for a closed beta. We want testers to enjoy the experience and feel like their actions matter, so that they stick around and continue to play, rather than test and grind. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/06b5a3684c815e1556434563e1f1564224b61f55.jpg"]

We believe that the results of a happy tester will have a much more lasting impact in the long run. While there are still some engineering milestones to hit before closed beta, the fun has already begun, and it will help closed beta be more impactful once started.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8c01d8aae9e0f4cf51f661bc06f25f7a6c034d7f.jpg"]

One of the major standouts in the update is how the game now loads maps, facilities, and enemies in a more dynamic and random fashion, resulting in gameplay that constantly changes and evolves throughout each mission. To do this, we needed more maps and facilities to load. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/14c0bfe2d1328f4f859ec95fc2661264897fe53d.jpg"]

Besides all the new facilities and parts that were designed, our artists created a new planet, one that is incredibly unique and unlike than anything we’ve seen in a game before. It feels dreamlike, and the influences from old sci-fi films and books are coming in full throttle.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/554f2bb59574a9555a74001535f51357680e1981.jpg"]

When we first brainstormed Warped Universe, we made a pact to create a universe that stands out. We want every screenshot to scream Warped Universe. This new planet and map do that more than ever before. We’re making a fun, exciting, and fresh game, and we’re beyond thrilled to be at this point in development.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/20eca8f9c3c6ca452e7d80018c1a093693aca5fd.jpg"]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - May 2025
notes.notes:
We covered all fronts this month at Warped Games, from game dev to marketing to backend infrastructure. One of the biggest wins was the momentum we’ve seen on our Steam page. We’ve spent the past six months consistently updating it with new content, visuals, and community posts. That kind of work doesn’t pay off immediately, it takes time, iteration, and a lot of convincing to get people to hit that Wishlist button. But this month, it clicked.

Thanks to a strong marketing push, more eyes are landing on Warped Universe, and more people are deciding it’s worth a spot on their wishlist. What’s even more exciting is that those numbers are now growing organically, players are discovering the game through other Steam pages, features, and community recommendations. That’s hugely rewarding, and we’ll keep building on that visibility with regular updates and gameplay reveals.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0fc41f40221a09f57c92fc20a4c0879b3aa3bca1.png
This month we focused heavily on ships, both player and Void. Void ships used to be simple palette-swapped versions of player ships. That’s now completely changed. Our art and design teams worked together to create an entirely new aesthetic for the Void, pulling more from their origin in the lore and pushing them into something far more eerie and distinct. The new models look truly warped and hostile, exactly as they should!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9dfa4309393c8103a9dbb93468d6c002b363b0e4.jpg
Player ships got a major upgrade too. We added loads of new cosmetic parts (like sails, tails, tusks, wings, hulls, masks, and auras), and reworked ship materials across all five battlepass tiers. These changes give players much more control over their visual identity in the universe. We also introduced new aura FX and a modular base system for internal ship skeletons to support even more variations in the future.

A lot of time this month went into tightening gameplay systems and combat feedback. Ammo was removed from player weapons to streamline combat, and damage numbers have been added for both player and enemy hits. This alone makes encounters feel more readable and reactive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/adf4c006f9b7ee20299a36d495bc6a999430a96a.png
On the backend side, we synced our latest work with Beamable and continued expanding tools and systems for development. Niagara FX scripts and emitters were pushed to handle new skeletal effects, and we laid the groundwork for future mission interactions by building a flexible base to build them on top of.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cdc2c173da17d46d3ed071f7cba6ce3c2e2394c.png
That’s it for this month’s game development update. We’re making Warped Universe deeper, sharper, and more reactive across the board. Thanks for continuing to follow the journey, whether you're here for the lore, the systems, or just to watch the ships explode in style, we’re glad you’re along for the ride.

Wishlist us on Steam if you haven’t already, and let us know what you think in the comments or on Discord!
